$comment: What JARVIS may do. Copy this file to ~/.jarvis/policy.json (or point JARVIS_POLICY at a copy) and edit it there; a policy file there replaces this one entirely.

Each entry is an exact tool name, or a pattern where * stands for the rest of one part of the name (it never crosses the __ between server and tool). Precedence: deny, then confirm, then allow. A tool on no list is denied, and the bridge prints every such tool at startup so you can decide where it belongs.

Prefer exact names. A pattern like mcp__x__get* also admits get_or_delete, which is the guessing-from-names this file replaces. The whole-server entries below are search services whose every tool is a lookup; list the tools of anything else one by one.
confirm: the action waits for you to press Enter on screen. Without --writes those tools are refused outright.
publicServers: MCP servers whose results are public (search, generation). Every other server's results count as private and switch on the leak guard.
trustedHosts: hosts JARVIS may reach even after private data is in the conversation. Subdomains are included.
